evidenceStatus: Fresh internal exact-target dispositions for commit 70091b642006f0b2788bd89a6a0e734a632619cf from Slither 0.11.5 and Aderyn 0.6.8. Every emitted instance was manually traced against this source target. This evidence is neither an independent audit nor release clearance.

internal-protocol-security.name: GUM BALL 6900 internal red team
internal-protocol-security.role: Internal exact-target analyzer triage; not an independent audit

rationales.slither:assembly: Both instances are the reviewed Fund EIP-1153 helpers: one memory-safe tstore and one memory-safe tload over a domain-separated duplicate-selection key. They do not access ordinary storage or arbitrary memory.
rationales.slither:calls-loop: The state-changing loops are fixed at sixteen reward tokens or caller-selected batches with scalar or omission fallbacks; Fund lets a redeemer exclude a broken asset, SignalGBX retains scalar add/remove, and Bribe retains scalar-token claims. SignalPortfolioLens loops are read-only discovery only.
rationales.slither:cyclomatic-complexity: Mine._validateResonanceRouter is intentionally a fail-closed view validator for every reciprocal identity in a future revenue graph. Each external getter is isolated by try/catch and any missing code, revert, or mismatch rejects the owner-only Router update before state changes.
rationales.slither:incorrect-equality: Runtime equalities are exact zero-amount state-machine sentinels; launcher equalities deliberately enforce pristine, exact genesis custody and final graph state. Unexpected Pair state aborts the unused launch atomically, and the documented recovery is a fresh launcher with different caller-scoped CREATE2 outputs.
rationales.slither:missing-inheritance: BribeRouter intentionally does not claim IResonanceRouter conformance: both expose route(), but one buffers an arbitrary Strategy payment token into a Bribe while the other buffers USDG into Resonance and has different identity and threshold semantics.
rationales.slither:missing-zero-check: Mine.genesisAuthority intentionally accepts zero as the permanent opt-out from genesis issuance. A zero authority can never satisfy msg.sender in mintGenesisLiquidity, while a nonzero canonical launcher authority is consumed and cleared before the fixed mint call.
rationales.slither:naming-convention: IBribe.REWARD_DURATION and IResonance.REWARD_DURATION intentionally match Solidity's generated getter names for public uppercase constants. Renaming either interface member would break exact ABI conformance rather than improve safety.
rationales.slither:reentrancy-benign: Mine and Strategy reports sit beneath nonReentrant and call immutable canonical dependencies; Resonance.addStrategy is nonReentrant and constructs an unregistered fresh graph through permanently bound factories. Reentrant mutation cannot cross the active guard, and any later failure rolls back the complete transition.
rationales.slither:reentrancy-events: The two findings concern only events emitted after successful downstream calls. BribeRouter has no mutable accounting state, and Resonance merely mirrors the canonical Bribe registration event after a call that performs no reward-token interaction; callback log ordering cannot change balances or authority.
rationales.slither:reentrancy-no-eth: Mine.mine and Strategy.buy are nonReentrant and use canonical immutable graph contracts. Launcher helpers execute only inside launch's active guard after launched is set, expose only a read-only partial deployment record during execution, and must pass exhaustive final assertions or atomically revert.
rationales.slither:timestamp: Block time is the specified input to mining emission accrual, hourly replacement auctions, Strategy auctions, deadlines, and seven-day streams. Exact boundary branches cap or finish each schedule; timestamp influence cannot bypass ownership, payment maxima, epoch identity, lifetime caps, or signal accounting.
rationales.slither:uninitialized-local: Mine.configuredSignalGBX is assigned only in the successful return branch of resonance.signalGBX(); the catch branch always reverts. The value is then required to contain code and pass reciprocal GBX and Resonance identity checks before the Router can be stored.
rationales.slither:unused-return: Strategy intentionally ignores distributeRevenue's convenience amount and snapshots its complete USDG balance so direct donations are included. The launcher intentionally ignores only getReserves' timestamp because exact reserve amounts and token ordering are the asserted genesis properties.
rationales.aderyn:centralization-risk: The findings enumerate the intended narrow administration: Mine may redirect future revenue only after reciprocal validation; Resonance has bounded Strategy, reward-token, Bribe-share, and one-time Router setup actions; setup-only owners can bind three shells once. Canonical launch renounces the shells and begins two-step Mine and Resonance transfers, while deployment remains blocked until reviewed governance accepts both.
rationales.aderyn:costly-loop: Both Bribe loops are bounded in code by the append-only maximum of sixteen reward tokens. An account can use claimReward for one token when an all-token claim is too costly or one reward token is broken.
rationales.aderyn:large-numeric-literal: The four literals are named, unit-documented constants: the 10,000 basis-point denominators in Mine, Resonance, and Strategy, plus the exact 100,000 ether genesis GBX Strategy price. Their values and units are intentional protocol configuration.
rationales.aderyn:local-variable-shadowing: The reported names are fields of Strategy.Config, not ambiguous executable locals. The constructor validates each field and assigns it explicitly to the same-named immutable or initial state variable under normal Solidity member scoping.
rationales.aderyn:missing-inheritance: BribeRouter intentionally remains distinct from IResonanceRouter despite sharing a route() selector: its immutable destination is a Bribe, its asset is a Strategy payment token, and its eligibility checks use Bribe reward state rather than Resonance revenue state.
rationales.aderyn:modifier-used-only-once: Resonance.onlyResonanceRouter names and centralizes the sole immutable revenue-source authorization used by notifyRevenue. Inlining the same check would be a style change with no security or gas-liveness consequence.
rationales.aderyn:non-reentrant-not-first: Mine.setResonanceRouter applies onlyOwner before nonReentrant. OpenZeppelin onlyOwner performs a storage comparison and no external call, so it cannot reenter or mutate state before the guard is entered.
rationales.aderyn:reentrancy-state-change: Constructor and reciprocal-binding findings use STATICCALL identity reads before exposure or one-time writes. Runtime value paths are nonReentrant or effects-first; Resonance's Strategy creation uses bound factories, and launcher launch is guarded with launched set before external work. Every failure reverts atomically.
rationales.aderyn:require-revert-in-loop: Atomic rejection is intentional: Fund must reject any invalid or inexact selected payout, SignalGBX batches must preserve one-for-one custody, and Resonance convenience claims must not partially advance checkpoints. Users retain single-asset redemption selection, scalar signal operations, and scalar Bribe token claims; Bribe's internal loops are capped at sixteen.
rationales.aderyn:state-no-address-check: Mine.genesisAuthority is the documented exception to zero-address rejection: zero permanently disables the optional fixed genesis issuance. The mint entry requires msg.sender to equal the authority and therefore cannot be reached through the zero address.
rationales.aderyn:storage-array-memory-edit: Mine.currentPrice deliberately copies one Slot from storage into the read-only _price memory parameter. _price performs no writes and is shared with the replacement path's already-snapshotted prior Slot, so no storage update is expected or lost.
rationales.aderyn:unchecked-return: Bribe.claimRewards ignores _claim's returned amount because _claim itself clears the entitlement, requests the SafeERC20 transfer, emits the payment event, and reverts atomically on failure. Strategy ignores distributeRevenue's amount because the following USDG balance snapshot is intentionally authoritative and includes donations.
rationales.aderyn:unused-public-function: Bribe.earned is an intentional permissionless accounting view for wallets, monitoring, and claim previews. Whether it is compiled as public or external is an ABI/gas style choice and does not expose mutation or authority.
rationales.aderyn:unused-state-variable: All eight reported values are private constant CREATE2 salt domains. Each is passed to _salt(msg.sender, domain) in its stateless component deployer; Aderyn failed to recognize those uses. Distinct domains and caller scoping prevent cross-component or cross-caller address consumption.

transient-redemption-marks.impact: Incorrect transient key derivation or clearing could admit duplicate selected assets or couple independent Fund redemptions within one transaction.
transient-redemption-marks.exploitability: The reviewed blocks contain only tstore and tload over keccak256(REDEMPTION_NAMESPACE, token); successful processing clears each mark and any revert transactionally discards transient state.
affectedAssumptions: The target chain and configured EVM continue to implement EIP-1153 semantics.
Fund remains nonReentrant and keeps its transient namespace domain separated.
transient-redemption-marks.revisitTrigger: Re-review if key derivation, mark lifetime, clearing order, compiler, target EVM, or redemption reentrancy changes.
compensatingControls: Tests cover duplicate orderings and repeated redemptions through one outer transaction.
The exact two Semgrep assembly locations are separately pinned and any movement fails the static gate.

liveness-preserving-loops.impact: An unbounded interaction loop could make a required signal exit, reward claim, or Fund redemption unavailable within the chain gas limit.
liveness-preserving-loops.exploitability: Reward loops are capped at sixteen; caller-controlled convenience batches can be split; scalar SignalGBX add/remove and Bribe token claims remain; Fund callers choose and may omit problematic assets; lens loops are read-only.
affectedAssumptions: Bribe reward registration remains capped at sixteen tokens in bytecode.
Scalar signal and reward paths and caller-selected Fund asset omission remain available.
liveness-preserving-loops.revisitTrigger: Re-review if a cap rises, a scalar or omission fallback is removed, a loop body gains material work, or chain gas limits change materially.
compensatingControls: Maximum-token and batch tests exercise bounded claim and signal paths.
Exit invariants exercise killed-Strategy scalar removals and redemption with omitted assets.

replacement-graph-validation.impact: A control-flow or assignment omission could install a future revenue Router with incompatible USDG, Fund, GBX, Resonance, or SignalGBX identities.
replacement-graph-validation.exploitability: The helper is view-only and fail-closed: every candidate has code, every identity read is caught, every reciprocal value is checked, and configuredSignalGBX is assigned only on the non-reverting return path before storage changes.
affectedAssumptions: Reciprocal identity getters remain the selected compatibility proof rather than a bytecode-honesty proof.
The Router update continues to affect only future protocol-share deposits.
replacement-graph-validation.revisitTrigger: Re-review if a graph identity, try/catch branch, migration scope, or Router setter authorization changes.
compensatingControls: Negative tests cover missing code, reverting getters, zero returns, and every reciprocal mismatch.
The old graph is never called or mutated by the future-revenue switch.

exact-sentinels-and-launch-state.impact: A mistaken strict comparison could skip value accounting, accept contaminated genesis custody, or leave an apparently canonical launch with incorrect locked liquidity.
exact-sentinels-and-launch-state.exploitability: Runtime comparisons are exact zero-state gates; launch comparisons are deliberate fail-closed assertions. Contamination or a preexisting Pair denies only an unused launch transaction, which rolls back before exposure and is recoverable with a fresh launcher graph.
affectedAssumptions: Canonical genesis continues to require exact USDG, GBX, reserve, supply, and locked-LP quantities.
Operators abandon a denied unused launcher and deploy a fresh caller-scoped address graph.
exact-sentinels-and-launch-state.revisitTrigger: Re-review if zero semantics, seed quantities, Pair adoption policy, CREATE2 scoping, or launch recovery changes.
compensatingControls: Genesis tests assert exact balances, reserves, total supply, locked LP, and atomic rollback.
Runtime boundary tests cover zero and neighboring nonzero amounts in each reported branch.

reviewed-interface-and-api-shape.impact: A mistaken interface, authorization helper, constant getter, or monitoring view could route the wrong asset, break integration, or obscure a caller restriction.
reviewed-interface-and-api-shape.exploitability: The reported declarations are deliberate: the two Router types have different identities, uppercase members match generated constant getters, onlyResonanceRouter names one source check, and Bribe.earned is a read-only public API.
affectedAssumptions: Consumers distinguish BribeRouter from ResonanceRouter by their canonical graph identities.
Constant getter selectors and permissionless accounting previews remain supported ABI surface.
reviewed-interface-and-api-shape.revisitTrigger: Re-review if a Router interface, constant visibility, modifier body, monitoring ABI, or integration typing changes.
compensatingControls: Deployment assertions pin each Router token and destination.
Compilation, authorization, and reward-preview tests exercise each reported ABI surface.

optional-genesis-authority.impact: An unintended zero authority could prevent fixed genesis issuance, while an unintended live authority could retain an extra mint path.
optional-genesis-authority.exploitability: Zero is explicitly the permanent disable setting and cannot originate a call. A nonzero authority can direct exactly one fixed mint only after Mine is the locked GBX minter, and the authority is cleared before interaction.
affectedAssumptions: Zero genesisAuthority continues to mean irreversible genesis issuance opt-out.
The nonzero canonical authority remains single-use and fixed to GENESIS_LIQUIDITY_GBX.
optional-genesis-authority.revisitTrigger: Re-review if genesis issuance amount, authorization, recipient checks, clearing order, or optional-zero semantics changes.
compensatingControls: Tests cover zero-disabled authority, wrong callers, repeat calls, and rollback on GBX failure.
Canonical final assertions require the authority cleared and genesisLiquidityMinted true.

guarded-and-static-callbacks.impact: A genuine callback window could duplicate a purchase or mint, corrupt signal and revenue weights, or expose a partially authorized deployment graph.
guarded-and-static-callbacks.exploitability: Reported identity reads are STATICCALLs or constructor-time; runtime value paths have active nonReentrant guards, effects-first state, or no post-call accounting. Launcher sets launched before guarded external work, and onlyOwner does no external work before Mine's guard.
affectedAssumptions: Canonical immutable GBX, Resonance, factories, Bribes, and stateless deployers retain reviewed bytecode.
Supported payment and reward assets follow the documented standard non-rebasing ERC-20 model.
guarded-and-static-callbacks.revisitTrigger: Re-review on any external-call reordering, new mutating entry point, guard removal, dependency mutability, event semantics, or supported-token model change.
compensatingControls: Callback-token and hostile-deployment tests require complete rollback and unchanged accounting.
Launcher final assertions and one-transaction atomicity reject incomplete or inconsistent graphs.

time-driven-state-machines.impact: Timestamp influence at a boundary can change one auction price, deadline result, emission interval, or stream checkpoint.
time-driven-state-machines.exploitability: Time is the intended monotonic input; all reported paths enforce explicit starts, finishes, maximum payments, expected epochs, fixed durations, and lifetime admission caps. No authorization or randomness derives from timestamp.
affectedAssumptions: Target-chain timestamps remain monotonic with ordinary sequencer or validator drift.
No economic rule requires precision finer than one block timestamp second.
time-driven-state-machines.revisitTrigger: Re-review if timestamp source, schedule duration, boundary inequality, deadline, price, or reward arithmetic changes.
compensatingControls: Boundary tests cover exact start, deadline, finish, overdue, halving, and neighboring timestamps.
Invariant campaigns reconcile cumulative supply and scheduled rewards across arbitrary time advances.

non-authoritative-returns.impact: Ignoring an authoritative result could hide a partial transfer, stale reserve, or incomplete reward claim.
non-authoritative-returns.exploitability: Each ignored value is deliberately non-authoritative: complete token balance is the Strategy snapshot, _claim performs its own state and transfer effects, and only V2 reserve quantities and ordering matter rather than the reserve timestamp.
affectedAssumptions: SafeERC20 failures continue to revert atomically for supported tokens.
Direct Strategy USDG donations remain intentionally included in the next purchase.
non-authoritative-returns.revisitTrigger: Re-review if any return gains independent success semantics, reserve freshness becomes relevant, or balance-snapshot purchase semantics changes.
compensatingControls: Tests assert complete Strategy balance delivery, scalar and aggregate claims, and exact seeded reserves.
Failures roll back entitlement clearing and every dependent state change.

bounded-administration-and-setup.impact: Compromise or misconfiguration of temporary setup ownership or continuing Mine and Resonance governance could redirect future revenue or alter Strategy and reward participation within the bounded admin surface.
bounded-administration-and-setup.exploitability: Mine cannot move old-graph funds and validates a replacement graph; Resonance rates are globally bounded and prospective; factories and SignalGBX bind once. Launch removes three setup owners but only begins two-step continuing ownership transfers.
affectedAssumptions: Production remains blocked until the exact external governance integration is reviewed and accepts both pending ownership transfers.
No new pause, rescue, arbitrary-call, upgrade, or claim-redirection authority is added.
bounded-administration-and-setup.revisitTrigger: Re-review when governance is selected or if ownership receipts, privileged methods, bounds, factory binding, or Router migration scope changes.
compensatingControls: Launch assertions require setup-shell owners zero and exact pending continuing owners.
Access-control tests enumerate privileged methods, invalid callers, bounds, and one-time setup consumption.

reviewed-configuration-shape.impact: An incorrect denominator, genesis price, or configuration-field assignment would deterministically misallocate payments or misconfigure every Strategy auction.
reviewed-configuration-shape.exploitability: The numeric findings are named, unit-documented constants; the shadowing findings are Config struct members explicitly validated and assigned through config.member under unambiguous Solidity member scoping.
affectedAssumptions: Ten thousand remains the common basis-point denominator and the GBX genesis Strategy price remains 100,000 ether.
Strategy construction continues to validate and explicitly assign every Config field.
reviewed-configuration-shape.revisitTrigger: Re-review if payment splits, launch prices, token units, Config layout, or constructor assignments change.
compensatingControls: Unit and launch tests pin rate boundaries, split complements, Config validation, and exact initial Strategy parameters.

read-only-slot-copy.impact: If _price were expected to mutate a live Slot, an implicit memory copy would silently discard the update and could misprice replacements.
read-only-slot-copy.exploitability: _price is view-only arithmetic over initialPrice and auctionStartedAt. Both currentPrice and mine intentionally use snapshots and all actual Slot writes remain explicit elsewhere.
affectedAssumptions: Auction quoting remains a pure read of the Slot snapshot and current timestamp.
No checkpoint or mutation is moved into _price.
read-only-slot-copy.revisitTrigger: Re-review if _price loses view semantics, gains a mutable field, or participates in Slot checkpointing.
compensatingControls: Price tests cover start, hourly decay, terminal zero, replacement, and stored next-epoch values.

caller-scoped-create2-domains.impact: Removing or colliding a salt domain could let one public deployer caller consume another component address or shift a canonical launcher's predicted graph.
caller-scoped-create2-domains.exploitability: Every reported constant is referenced in a CREATE2 salt derived from abi.encode(msg.sender, domain); domains are contract-specific and deployers retain no state or authority.
affectedAssumptions: Each component type retains a unique literal domain string.
The direct caller remains included in every deployer salt derivation.
caller-scoped-create2-domains.revisitTrigger: Re-review if a domain string, _salt encoding, caller scope, CREATE opcode, or deployer state changes.
compensatingControls: Prediction tests compare caller-specific outputs and reject cross-caller address consumption.
Canonical launcher final assertions pin the complete deployed graph before success.
